content: Realize deeply that the present moment is all you have. Make the NOW the primary focus of your life.
author: Eckhart Tolle
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

In Eckhart Tolle's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: Where can you bring full, undistracted presence into an ordinary routine or conversation today?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
